headline: Hydration is maintaining water levels—every cell needs water to function properly
universal_truth: The obvious things are often the most important; basic maintenance enables everything else
fun_facts: Even 2% dehydration impairs cognitive performance and physical capability
Your brain is about 75% water—hydration directly affects thinking
Thirst often indicates you're already mildly dehydrated—drink before you're thirsty
discussion_questions: How well do you maintain basic needs like hydration?
What obvious fundamentals do you neglect?
What happens to your performance when basics slip?

hook.script: Water seems boring, basic, obvious. Yet every chemical reaction in your body requires it. Dehydrate even slightly, and thinking fogs, energy drops, performance suffers. The most basic things are often the most important.

cliff.script: We chase complex solutions while neglecting simple fundamentals. What does hydration teach about basics?
cliff.prompt: Why do basics matter so much?

options.text: Basics enable everything else—without foundational needs met, sophisticated capabilities fail; the most impactful improvements are often the most boring
options.response: Yes. No amount of advanced technique compensates for dehydration. Fundamentals must be in place before fancy strategies matter. Boring basics are often the highest-leverage improvements.

options.text: Water is just essential for life
options.response: Essential, yes, but the broader principle is that fundamentals enable everything else...

fact1.title: Foundation First
fact1.script: Water is foundation—without it, nothing else works. You can't optimize what isn't fueled. Check basics before seeking advanced solutions. Often the answer is boring but essential.

fact2.title: Invisible Deficits
fact2.script: Mild dehydration often goes unnoticed. You feel 'off' without knowing why. Performance suffers from invisible causes. Check the obvious before diagnosing the obscure.

fact3.title: Maintenance Is Invisible
fact3.script: Good hydration gets no credit—you just function. Only failure is noticed. This is true for all maintenance: sleep, nutrition, relationships. Invisible work enables visible performance.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The obvious things are often the most important. Basic maintenance enables everything else. Don't neglect fundamentals.

outro.script: That's Day 309. Tomorrow, we'll explore preparing your body—warm-up and stretching. Until then, drink some water.

growTrack.title: Fundamentals Check - What Basics Are You Neglecting?
growTrack.activity: What basics do you neglect—sleep, water, nutrition, rest, connection? These are boring but essential. Which fundamental, if maintained, would most improve your performance? Focus there first.
